name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 2, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on February 2, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 28, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht
Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there are no Closed Session agenda items this evening.

RECESS

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  February 2, 2015
 INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Schlicht

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the Mission Viejo High School Marching Band and Color Guard for
  Placing Third in the Western Band Association State Championship

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of commendation to the MVHS Marching Band and
  Color Guard.

P2.  Recognize the 2014 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Schlicht presented plaques to (1) Senior Public Services Contracts Administrator,
  Chris Covellone, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Deputy Matt Anderson,
  Orange County Sheriff's Department Employee of the Year; and (3) Fire Fighter, Chuck
  Hawkins, Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bob Hayes, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Community of Character, he shared copies of the
character newsletters that are distributed to every school in the City. He invited the Council
Members and residents to attend the February character film, The 99ers', which will be shown in
the City Council Chamber on Sunday, February 15 beginning at 2:00 p.m. Lastly, Mr. Hayes
announced that the Honor Flight program sends WWII Veterans back to Washington DC to tour
the monuments and on February 16, 2015, 20% of purchases made at California Pizza Kitchen will
be donated to the Honor Flight program.

Rob Bannis, M.V.: announced that the Nadadores program was the primary reason he moved from
Topeka, Kansas to Mission Viejo. He shared his personal story of the time he spent swimming for
the Nadadores, attending Mission Viejo schools, and that he and his wife established permanent
residence in Mission Viejo to raise their family. Mr. Bannis requested that the Council support
the restoration of the Marguerite Aquatics Center as an essential and valuable community service.

Chuck McCullough, M.V.: invited the City Council Members to February Chamber of Commerce
events, including ribbon cutting ceremonies for Driving Miz Daisy Vintage Market and the Auto
Club. He also announced that the Chamber's monthly mixer will be held on February 19, 2015,
from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at Pizza Studio.

Roger Young, Vice President of the Nadadores Foundation, Trabuco Canyon: thanked the City
Council for its past support and he distributed newsletters and information on the Nadadores'
programs covering the last three years.

City Council Minutes  2  February 2, 2015
 Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: provided a history of the plan for bocce ball courts at the Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center and she asked the City Council to support the installation of the
courts.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that there is a swimming pool hanging in mid-air over the houses
on Ferrocarril Street. She encouraged the City Council Members to drive by and take a look and
to make sure that the City has declared it technically safe.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 3 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

4.  Check Register Dated January 16, 2015 in the Amount of $637,980.52

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  2014 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

City Council Minutes  3  February 2, 2015
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the tenor of the January 16 budget
  workshop minutes. She stated that the Council's consensus was to get the cost of programs
  before agreeing to set anything in stone.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) approve the
  Minutes for the City Council Workshop of January 16, 2015, as presented, and (2) approve
  the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of January 19, 2015, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

3.  Check Register Dated January 9, 2015 in the Amount of $2,026,243.40.

  Mayor Schlicht noted a payment on page 4 to DHL Express USA for ITF expenses. She
  stated that the Council hasn't given direction to support a 2015 ITF event and she wants to
  make sure that the staff isn't committing the City to host the event.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

6.  Agreement to add Food & Wine component to Arts Alive Festival

  Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen presented the staff report and
  answered the City Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  authorize City Staff to negotiate and approve an agreement with EventWerks for provision
  of a Food & Wine Festival component at this year's Arts Alive Festival, May 2 and 3, 2015.
City Council Minutes  4  February 2, 2015
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

7.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

8.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

9.  Implementing Park Restroom Master Plan

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report on
  behalf of the Community Services Commission.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  confirm that the City Council would like the Community Services Commission to begin
  community outreach and other research for constructing restrooms at Pavion Park and
  Cordova Park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Schlicht asked that staff clarify the Little Leagues' concerns that they were not part
  of the discussion. She also requested that residents are shown an example of what the
  proposed park restrooms might look like.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  5  February 2, 2015
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including the Jennie Finch
Softball Camp where Mayor Schlicht caught the first pitch and the grand opening of Evolution
Swim Academy which is owned by former Olympian and Nadadores member, Felipe Delgado,
and four investors who were also Olympians. Council Member Bucknum stated that the she
appreciated the Nadadores presentation earlier in the meeting and she believes that youth sports
and activities provide inspiration to children. She also believes in supporting organizations that
promote youth activities and said that she feels very passionately about that. Council Member
Bucknum noted that her son Spencer was recognized this evening with the Mission Viejo High
School band and it was a very proud moment for her. Lastly, Council Member Bucknum asked
staff to define when they will need direction from the Council on the ITF Wheelchair Tennis
Masters for 2015.

Council Member Sachs

11.  Resolution Opposing the Potential Closure of the Saddleback Memorial Care San
  Clemente Campus

  Council Member Sachs presented his report.

  Tony Struthers, Administrator of Saddleback Memorial Care, San Clemente: stated that
  they are looking at ways to change the hospital from an in-patient facility to an out-patient
  facility. He presented additional wording and asked the Council to consider adding it to
  the proposed resolution to support legislation for free standing emergency rooms.

  Dr. Steven Cullen, San Clemente: stated that he is a doctor on staff at both San Clemente
  and Mission hospitals. He expressed his opposition to the closure of Saddleback hospital,
  San Clemente campus, and asked the Council for their support.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 15-06 (as amended) Opposing the Potential Closure of the Saddleback
  Memorial Care San Clemente Campus.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  February 2, 2015
 12.  Recommendation to Repeal SFPA (Special Fire Protection Area): Adopt Ordinance
  and Resolution for Repeal While Maintaining Public Safety

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

  The following spoke in support of the proposal: Rhonda Reardon, M.V. (contingent upon
  written assurances) and Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposal: Debbie Peel, M.V.; Rita Tayanaka,
  M.V.; and Dennis O’Connor, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to introduce
  Ordinance 15-304 Repealing Ordinance 12-294 In Part, As It Previously Repealed
  Ordinance 95-151 (Designation Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones) And Amended Its
  Ordinance 10-287 To Delete The Defined Terms "Fire Hazard Severity Zones", "Local
  Agency Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone" And "Wildland-Urban Interface Fire Area"
  And In All Instances Of Use Substituting The Term "Special Fire Protection Area" Or
  "SFPA", For All Purposes, As Further Defined Herein.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to call the question.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Bucknum
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Congratulated the employees of the year who were recognized earlier in the meeting. He also
thanked the two gentlemen from the Nadadores who came to help educate the Council on the
Nadadores program.

Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht stated that she would like to ask for Council consensus to have the Planning and
Transportation Commission direct the traffic subcommittee to study traffic issues by looking at

City Council Minutes  7  February 2, 2015
 flow-based and time-based technologies that are available. She also stated that she feels strongly
about setting up a youth center and would like to have the Community Services Commission look
at repurposing the Potocki Center or the Felipe Tennis Center. It would not be a city-run program
but a building that the City could offer for a private company to run. She asked that the
Commission Chairman appoint Grant Voss due to his CUSD contacts and his youthfulness, along
with third generation resident Joe Tully and Chairman Magill and that the committee return with
a recommendation in a 90-day period. Mayor Schlicht stated that she would also like to change
the Council Meeting time to 5:30 p.m. and change the date to Tuesdays and she asked that it be
placed on an agenda so Council can address the pros and cons. She further asked staff to provide
a list of the contracts that are expiring in May, June and July. Mayor Schlicht congratulated the
Mission Viejo High School marching band and color guard and she thanked the employees of the
year for their service. She also thanked all of the City volunteers for their time, talent and
knowledge. She announced that California Pizza Kitchen will host “Pizza With a Purpose” to
benefit the Honor Flight program and 20% of all receipts on February 16, 2015, will be donated to
Honor Flight. Mayor Schlicht mentioned the recent fire in a San Juan Capistrano condo and asked
if OCFA can make a presentation on the value of having a fire alarm system and rotating
batteries. She further stated that she is perplexed that the sports leagues are being led to believe
that fees to build park restrooms will be passed on to them and she clarified that it is park fees that
will pay for the restrooms. In closing, Mayor Schlicht read a quote from Abraham Lincoln: “In
all that the people can individually do as well for themselves, government ought not do for them.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:39 p.m. with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, February 16, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 16, 2015

City Council Minutes  8  February 2, 2015
